title: His eight children and keeping them out of show business
summary: McRae discourages his daughters from the road, remembering Ella's difficulties as a woman travelling.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: In the early 50's, who were some of the people you recorded with besides Wynona Harris?
I didn't record with too many people then. I was just writing.
Just writing, just gigging, doing my own thing.
How about your family? Your children must've been coming of age by this time.
Oh, yeah. My daughter was and college going to high school (inaudible). I was spending a lot of money on them.

How many children do you have?
I had five girls and three boys.

One of them -- they very -- they turn out -- I wasn't particular about wanting them to get into show business, because at that time the show business was so bad, you know. People were getting on dope and stuff, like that. That was the area that Big Mabel -- I just couldn't see -- and it was so hard for women to break through and the travelling was hard on them, you know. I remember what Ella went through the years we was on the road with Chick. It's really a rough thing for a girl vocalist on the road. Because the accommodations wasn't as --

up to what, you know, what you could get in a town, you know. You're moving so fast and you got to travel so long -- two hundred and fifty miles -- (inaudible) sometime three hundred miles overnight. We leave here and go all the way down south, you know. Go right in town to do a date maybe. It's really rough. So I just couldn't see -- I say, well -- let them see my kids getting into show business. (inaudible) do what they -- whatever they wanna do, that's correct. (inaudible). I won't encourage them, they wanted to (inaudible) take up medicine and they was doing good.
